title: Proteome analyses for the prediction of complications in thoracic aortic dissections
summary:
Thoracic Standford type B aortic dissections (STBAD) are life-threatening diseases in which the inner wall layer of the aorta is split open by a tear, allowing blood to enter the middle layer of the aortic wall. This leads to a “false” lumen that expands longitudinally. 40% of STBAD patients treated with intensive care develop complications with high mortality and morbidity. The progression of the disease has so far been monitored by non-specific laboratory parameters and CT angiography, which expose patients to higher radiation doses and longer hospital stays. 
Proteome analyses will be used to identify specific changes in the protein “pattern” during the course of the disease. The aim is to identify patients at increased risk and treat them at an early stage, and to reduce the radiation exposure in patients with uncomplicated STBAD.
conditions: Proteom analysis, STBAD, Aortic dissection (any part)

interventions.name:
Patients with Stanford type B aortic dissection (STBAD) are routinely provided with intensive medical care, unless there is an emergency indication for a TEVAR.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Written consent to participate in the study (HeiPoDD study information + information on proeteome analyses for the prediction of complications in thoracic aortic dissections)
- Age > 18 years
- Radiologically confirmed evidence of a thoracic aortic dissection Stanford type B
- Capacity to consent
- The control patients from the HeiPoDD study consented to inclusion in the HeiPoDD study
Exclusion criteria:
- Age < 18 years
- Cancellation/refusal of the radiological examination
- Lack of written consent from the patient
